body.heading: Sit and listen
paragraphs: Find a quiet outdoor spot with your adult and sit down together. Close your eyes if you like — ears work wonderfully on their own.
Birds sing to talk to each other. A song can mean this is my tree, or it can be a call to a friend. Every kind of bird has its own tune.

body.heading: Count the songs
paragraphs: Listen for one minute. Every time you hear a new kind of song, make a mark on your paper. A whistle, a chirp, and a trill are three different songs.
Some birds repeat their song like a stuck record. Others sing a whole jumbled concert. Which singer is the loudest? Which is the quietest?

body.heading: Morning is best
paragraphs: Birds sing most in the early morning. Scientists call it the dawn chorus — a whole orchestra warming up as the sun rises.
Try listening at different times of day. Your marks will show you when your garden is at its most musical.

takeaway: Every bird species sings its own song, and careful listening lets you count singers you cannot even see.
safetyNotes: Stay close to your adult and sit in a safe spot away from roads. Never try to touch birds or nests.
screenFreeExtension: Try to copy your favourite bird sound with your voice and see if your family can guess it.
